prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows an open outdoor paved courtyard sloped visually due to head tilt, with a metal rack holding blue trays in the bottom-left foreground of frame 1 at 0.5–1.5 m (within arm's reach) and flat ground receding from ~1.5 m near the bottom edge to over 20 m toward distant green-roofed buildings and horizon trees. In frame 2, a man in a red shirt enters centrally at very high brightness (~0.5–0.8 m, well within arm's reach), facing the camera wearer while looking slightly downward and occluding the background pole and ground behind him; in frame 3, he drops into the bottom-left corner at ~0.5 m as the camera wearer turns right, before appearing further away (~1.2–1.5 m, just outside comfortable arm's reach) in frame 4 facing right in profile, and returning to the bottom-left foreground (~0.6 m) in frame 5 with his left arm extended rightward within reach. The map also captures a thin vertical pole behind the man in frames 2–4 at roughly 3–5 m, sitting several metres behind him. Unlike the RGB image where harsh shadows on the stone tiles complicate distance perception, the depth map clearly separates the physical 3D foreground figure and upright pole from the flat ground plane and cast shadows. However, the map is unreliable along the open sky and distant horizon (>15 m) where depth saturates to uniform black, and inside the complex lattice of the metal rack in frame 1 where thin bars blend with the background.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates the man in the red shirt as a single foreground `person` mask in frames 2 through 5, while leaving the entire surrounding courtyard, drying trays, metal rack, poles, and distant sheds unsegmented in black. Across the sequence, this `person` mask shifts from occupying the central foreground in frame 2 (~0.5–0.8 m away, facing toward the camera wearer) to being heavily cropped at the bottom-left edge in frame 3 (~0.5 m, only shoulder and head edge visible), stepping back to ~1.2–1.5 m in frame 4 while turned right in profile, and moving back into the lower-left foreground (~0.6 m, within arm's reach) with his left arm reaching right in frame 5. The sharp mask silhouettes clearly delineate where the man's torso and head occlude the background pole and tiled ground, providing crisp figure-ground boundaries even where his dark hair overlaps dark background elements in RGB. However, the map is highly unreliable in frame 4 where it hallucinates a brown `person` mask on a dark ground shadow to the right (roughly 2–3 m away on the pavement), and in frame 5 where it misclassifies the two cast human shadows on the stone tiles (3–5 m ahead and to the right) as two separate `person` instances. It also fails to segment any non-person objects within arm's reach, such as the foreground metal rack in frame 1.
descriptions.pose: The skeleton map detects sparse upper-body and facial keypoints (yellow) for the man in the red shirt only in frames 2 and 4, while frames 1, 3, and 5 are completely empty black. In frame 2, when the man is ~0.5–0.8 m in front of the camera wearer and within arm's reach, facial landmarks (eyes, nose, ears) and a shoulder-to-elbow line show his torso angled toward the camera and his head tilted down and slightly left rather than looking directly into the lens. In frame 4, when he is ~1.2–1.5 m away to the left of center, a cluster of right-side facial keypoints and a narrowed shoulder line capture his 90-degree turn to his left (viewer's right), looking away from the camera wearer across the courtyard. This skeletal abstraction makes the exact head pitch and shoulder rotation between frames 2 and 4 immediately explicit without distractions from lighting or clothing, and unlike segmentation, it does not falsely trigger on the dark ground shadows in frames 4 and 5. However, the pose map is severely unreliable whenever the body is truncated by the frame boundary, completely missing the man's partial shoulder in frame 3, his close-up torso and outstretched left arm/hand in frame 5 (with zero magenta hand keypoints detected despite his wrist and hand being visible at the bottom edge), as well as his lower body across all frames.
